subject: pathology
title: Iron Deficiency Anaemia: Ferritin, Transferrin Saturation, and Mentzer Index

steps.tx: Iron deficiency evolves silently: stores empty first, then iron deficient erythropoiesis, then microcytic anaemia, so a normal haemoglobin never excludes depleted stores in a bleeding or pregnant patient. The storage protein whose serum level mirrors those stores is **serum ferritin**, low values proving deficiency.
steps.say: Ferritin falls before haemoglobin does; a normal haemoglobin never excludes empty iron stores.

vis.caption: Iron deficiency blood film with microcytic hypochromic red cells and pencil cells.

steps.tx: Transferrin saturation reports iron actually available to marrow: serum iron divided by total iron binding capacity falls below fifteen percent in deficiency while binding capacity rises as the liver makes more transferrin. The availability ratio is **transferrin saturation**, complementing ferritin when inflammation confuses it.
steps.say: Transferrin saturation below fifteen percent means the marrow is starved of iron today, whatever the stores claim.

steps.tx: The blood film narrates chronicity: microcytic hypochromic cells with pencil forms, anisopoikilocytosis, and a raised red cell distribution width as new small cells mix with older normal ones. Spoon shaped koilonychia nails and angular cheilitis complete the bedside picture of **iron deficiency anaemia**.
steps.say: Pencil cells, high RDW, spoon nails, and sore mouth corners narrate iron deficiency before any laboratory speaks.

vis.caption: Koilonychia spoon nails with peripheral smear features of iron deficiency.

steps.tx: Ferritin lies upward as an acute phase reactant, so inflammation, infection, liver disease, and malignancy can mask deficiency behind a normal value, prompting saturation, soluble receptor, or marrow iron assessment. Perls Prussian blue on marrow remains the reference standard; the stain is **Perls Prussian blue** for storage iron.
steps.say: Inflammation inflates ferritin dishonestly; when the story disagrees, trust saturation or stain the marrow with Perls blue.

steps.tx: In children, the Mentzer index, mean cell volume divided by red cell count, separates iron deficiency, index above thirteen, from thalassaemia trait, below thirteen, as a free first approximation before iron studies and haemoglobin analysis. The bedside ratio is the **Mentzer index**.
steps.say: Mentzer index above thirteen favours iron deficiency, below thirteen favours thalassaemia trait; confirm both properly.

nodes.label: Mentzer index: MCV divided by red cell count

steps.tx: Finding deficiency is half the duty; finding its source is the other half, because gastrointestinal blood loss from ulcers, malignancy, angiodysplasia, or hookworm explains most adult cases, with menstrual loss and malabsorption behind the rest. Iron replacement without source hunting misses cancers; that hunt is **iron deficiency source investigation**.
steps.say: Replace the iron, but hunt the leak; adult iron deficiency is gastrointestinal blood loss until proven otherwise.

steps.tx: Oral ferrous salts remain first line, taken away from tea, calcium, and acid suppression, with intravenous iron for intolerance, malabsorption, ongoing loss, or late pregnancy urgency. A haemoglobin rise of about ten grams per litre in two to four weeks confirms response; the monitored milestone is **haemoglobin response**.
steps.say: Expect haemoglobin up ten grams per litre within a month on iron; no rise means adherence, absorption, or ongoing loss problems.

left.title: Oral iron succeeds when
points: Taken away from tea and calcium

steps.tx: Pica, craving ice, clay, or raw rice, restless legs, and glossitis broaden recognition beyond pallor, especially in pregnancy and childhood where development suffers silently. Asking directly about cravings costs nothing and clinches suspicion; the craving syndrome is **pica of iron deficiency**.
steps.say: Ask about ice, clay, or raw rice cravings; pica and restless legs often announce iron deficiency before pallor does.
